spans.s:
Yevāṣa is the name of a destructive insect in the Atharvaveda.^1
The form Yavāṣa is found in the Kāṭhaka Saṃhitā.^2 Cf. Vṛṣa.
1) v. 23, 7. 8.
2) xxx. 1 (Indische Studien, 3, 462).
The same form occurs in the Gaṇas,
kumudādi and prekṣādi (Pāṇini, iv. 2,
80). Cf. Maitrāyaṇī Saṃhitā, iv. 8, 1,
where Yavāṣa should be read; Kapi-
ṣṭhala Saṃhitā, xlvi. 4.
Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 98;
St. Petersburg Dictionary, s.v.
